payload.scope:
i8c takes on:
- A top-middle board toolbar: a greyed book placeholder (until i6) + an active phone-connect icon.
- The connect action: clicking phone-connect generates the ntfy topic pair, writes ~/.se/<project>/phone.json (enabled), and renders a QR in the details pane, encoded LOCALLY.
- A correct local QR encoder (vendored or hand-rolled per se.adr-install-over-zerodep).
All against the existing i8 bless mechanics, unchanged. Runs in i8c's worktree, blessed on the board.
payload.non_goals:
- The book itself + its open action (i6; the icon ships greyed).
- Other toolbar icons (future, per feature).
- Non-ntfy channels.
- The i8 bless mechanics (unchanged).
- QR decoding / the inbound side (the phone app subscribes; we only ENCODE).
- Live owner-physical pairing (se.raid-phone-live-pairing).
payload.prfaq:
PRESS RELEASE (internal): Pair your phone in one click. The se board gains a phone-connect button; click it, a QR appears in the details pane, scan it with your ntfy app, and your phone is paired. Gate offers reach your pocket; one tap blesses from away. No config files; the topic is generated and drawn locally, never leaving your machine.

HOSTILE FAQ:
- Isn't a QR carrying a secret a leak? Encoded locally, shown only on your board; the topic IS the credential (se.adr-answer-authenticity).
- Why not a hosted QR service? It hands the topic to a third party. Refused.
- Heavy dependency? No - one-click install is the law; the encoder is vendored or hand-rolled, vetted at ship.
- Phone required? No - opt-in; without phone.json it is silent, unchanged from i8.
- Auth changed? No - i8's hash-bound, channel-stamped bless is untouched; i8c adds only the pairing gesture.
payload.findings_folded: None, with reason: no test or spike has run at M1. The QR encoder spike is M6; the red-first tests (connect action, encoder, toolbar) land at M7. Nothing to fold upstream.
